rows.question: When can a Singapore business recover input GST on purchases?
What conditions must a GST-registered business satisfy before claiming GST input tax?
Can a GST-registered company claim input tax on business purchases, and what records are needed?
Explain when a business may recover GST input tax on purchases used to make taxable supplies.
rows.before:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence is incomplete for one or more material issues.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** Additional case facts or checks are required; see the issue-level limitations.
**Material evidence gaps:** See the evidence gaps and coverage limitations below.

#### IRAS — GST

**Status:** Verified evidence; case application unresolved

**GST input tax claim eligibility and supporting documentation** (party in scope: Company)
- **IRAS rule explanation:** IRAS allows an input tax claim only when all applicable conditions are met: the claimant is GST-registered; the goods or services are supplied to or imported by it and are used for its business; local purchases have valid tax invoices and imports have the required import permits and supporting documents; the input tax is attributable to qualifying taxable or specified out-of-scope supplies; the claim is not disallowed under Regulations 26 or 27; and the claimant has taken reasonable steps to conclude that the goods or services are not part of a Missing Trader Fraud arrangement, on a conclusion a reasonable person would make. This gives the general rule only. A conclusion about a particular purchase also requires the GST-registration status, what was acquired and its business use, the related supplies, supporting documents, any applicable blocked-input-tax exception, and the Missing Trader Fraud assessment. [IRAS | Conditions for Claiming Input Tax](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-(gst)/claiming-gst-(input-tax)/conditions-for-claiming-input-tax)
- **Application unresolved:** For GST input tax claim eligibility and supporting documentation, case-specific treatment or calculation has not been verified. The relevant facts and statutory conditions still need to be established.

**Source:** IRAS | Conditions for Claiming Input Tax (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST input tax claim eligibility and supporting documentation): You can claim input tax incurred on your purchases only if all the following conditions are met:
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST input tax claim eligibility and supporting documentation): 1. You are GST-registered;
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST input tax claim eligibility and supporting documentation): 2. The goods or services are supplied to you or imported by you;
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST input tax claim eligibility and supporting documentation): 3. The goods or services are used or will be used for the purpose of your business;
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST input tax claim eligibility and supporting documentation): 4. Local purchases are supported by valid tax invoices addressed to you, or simplified tax invoices, at the time of claiming of the input tax;
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST input tax claim eligibility and supporting documentation): 5. Imports are supported by import permits that show that you are the importer of the goods and other supporting documents such as the supplier's invoices and relevant transport documents;
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST input tax claim eligibility and supporting documentation): 6. The input tax is directly attributable to taxable supplies (i.e. standard-rated supplies and zero-rated supplies), or out-of-scope supplies (e.g. third country sale of goods), that would be taxable supplies if made in Singapore;
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST input tax claim eligibility and supporting documentation): 7. The input tax claims are not disallowed under Regulations 26 and 27 of the GST (General) Regulations;
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST input tax claim eligibility and supporting documentation): 8. You have taken reasonable steps to ascertain and concluded that the goods or services were not part of a Missing Trader Fraud arrangement and the conclusion is one that a reasonable person would have made.
- Official source: [IRAS | Conditions for Claiming Input Tax](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-(gst)/claiming-gst-(input-tax)/conditions-for-claiming-input-tax)

### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence is incomplete for one or more material issues.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.

#### IRAS — GST

**Status:** Evidence verified

**GST return filing deadline, nil-return duty, and extension procedure** (party in scope: Company)
- **IRAS rule explanation:** A GST return and any tax due are generally due one month after the accounting period ends. A nil return is still required when there was no business activity. For GIRO, deduction is on the 15th of the month after the payment due date, shifted to the next working day if it falls on a weekend or public holiday. Extensions are generally not granted; IRAS considers only acceptable reasons, requires a request with supporting documents at least five working days before the due date, and if the request is not approved before the due date, late filing penalties apply and the outstanding GST F5 must be filed immediately. [GST Filing Due Dates and Requests for Extension | Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) (offline fixture title)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-(gst)/filing-gst/gst-filing-due-dates-and-requests-for-extension)

**Source:** GST Filing Due Dates and Requests for Extension | Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) (offline fixture title) (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports GST return filing deadline, nil-return duty, and extension procedure): You must file a “Nil” return even if you had no business activity during the accounting period.

Filing and payment due dates

Your GST return and payment are due 1 month after the end of your accounting period. If you pay via GIRO, IRAS will deduct payment on the 15th day of the month after the payment due date. If the deduction date falls on a weekend or public holiday, the deduction will be made on the next working day.

Without GIRO

GST Accounting Period  | File and pay by

Jan - Mar  | 30 Apr

Apr - Jun  | 31 Jul

Jul - Sept  | 31 Oct

Oct - Dec  | 31 Jan

With GIRO

GST Accounting Period  | File by | GIRO deduction Date

Jan - Mar  | 30 Apr  | 15 May

Apr - Jun  | 31 Jul  | 15 Aug

Jul - Sept  | 31 Oct  | 15 Nov

Oct - Dec  | 31 Jan  | 15 Feb

Note: To confirm that your GST will be paid via GIRO, check the acknowledgement page after you file your GST F5 return.

Filing due date for special accounting periods

If you have special GST accounting periods, your return is due 1 month after the end of that accounting period.

Example: If your period runs from 5 Apr 2026 to 5 Jul 2026, your return is due on 5 Aug 2026.

Penalties for late filing and payment

Penalties will apply if you are late in filing your GST return and making payment.

Requesting an extension to file

As one month after the end of your accounting period is a reasonable deadline, extensions are generally not granted. You are expected to maintain proper transaction tracking systems and ensure you have adequate resources to file on time.

Reasons that will not be accepted

No extension will be granted for the following reasons:

• Staff on maternity leave

• Director or key accounts personnel are overseas

• Staff have resigned without proper handover

• Closing of accounts at year-end

• New accounts personnel do not know how to handle GST matters

• No computer

• Not enough manpower to handle GST matters

Acceptable reasons for extension

We may grant an extension only if your request arises from one of the acceptable reasons below:

Acceptable reasons for extension | Documents required  | Maximum extension granted

Newly GST-registered businesses filing their first GST return  | Nil  | 1 month

Breakdown of IT system  | e.g. IT servicing report  | 2 weeks

Purchase of a new accounting software or IT system | Tax invoice | 2 weeks

Key accounting personnel on long medical leave (more than 1 week)  | Medical/ hospitalisation certificates  | 2 weeks

Restructuring of company  | e.g. Notice of restructuring, media release  | 2 weeks

Software issues or errors encountered when submitting GST returns via seamless filing software through API | Nil | 2 weeks

How to submit your request

Submit your extension request form at least 5 working days before the filing due date, together with all required supporting documents.

Note: Requests submitted late or after the filing due date will not be processed. If your request is not approved before the due date, late filing penalties will apply. You will also be required to file the outstanding GST F5 immediately.
- Official source: [GST Filing Due Dates and Requests for Extension | Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) (offline fixture title)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/goods-services-tax-(gst)/filing-gst/gst-filing-due-dates-and-requests-for-extension)

rows.before:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

#### IRAS — Corporate income tax

**Status:** Evidence verified

**Estimated Chargeable Income filing deadline and general waiver conditions** (party in scope: Company)
- **IRAS rule explanation:** IRAS generally requires ECI filing within three months after FYE. The general waiver requires both annual revenue of S$5 million or less for that financial year and nil ECI for the YA, with ECI measured before partial or start-up exemption. Revenue is the company’s main source of income; for an investment holding company it is investment income. A nil ECI or book loss alone does not qualify a company whose relevant revenue exceeds S$5 million; likewise, revenue below the threshold does not qualify when ECI is positive. IRAS gives separate entity categories that need not file and says companies self-assess the waiver. To assess a particular YA, confirm FYE, principal/investment revenue, pre-exemption ECI and any specifically excluded category. [IRAS | Estimated Chargeable Income (ECI) Filing](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/estimated-chargeable-income-(eci)-filing)

**Source:** IRAS | Estimated Chargeable Income (ECI) Filing (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Estimated Chargeable Income filing deadline and general waiver conditions): ECI is an estimate of your company's taxable profits (after deducting tax-allowable expenses) for a Year of Assessment (YA).
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Estimated Chargeable Income filing deadline and general waiver conditions): Your company has to file ECI within 3 months from the end of your financial year unless: • Your company qualifies for the ECI filing waiver; or • Your company is specifically not required to file ECI.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Estimated Chargeable Income filing deadline and general waiver conditions): Your company does not need to file ECI in any Year of Assessment (YA) when both criteria are met: • Annual revenue1 is $5 million or below for the financial year; and • ECI is nil for the YA. The ECI should be the amount before deducting the exempt amount under the partial tax exemption scheme or the tax exemption scheme for new start-up companies.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Estimated Chargeable Income filing deadline and general waiver conditions): Revenue refers to a company's main source of income and excludes separate source income, such as interest, dividend and rental, which does not arise from its principal activity. In the case of an investment holding company, the revenue is its investment income (e.g. dividend income and interest income).
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Estimated Chargeable Income filing deadline and general waiver conditions): Your company is required to self-assess if it qualifies for the ECI filing waiver.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Estimated Chargeable Income filing deadline and general waiver conditions): If your company falls within 1 of the following categories, it does not need to file ECI: • Foreign ship owners or charterers whose local shipping agent has submitted/ will submit the Shipping Return (PDF, 104KB) • Foreign universities • Designated unit trusts and approved CPF unit trusts# • Real estate investment trusts that have been granted the tax treatment under Section 43(2) of the Income Tax Act 1947 • Cases specifically granted the waiver to furnish ECI by IRAS
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Estimated Chargeable Income filing deadline and general waiver conditions): If your company's ECI is nil and its annual revenue is more than $5 million, you are still required to file the ECI.
- Official source: [IRAS | Estimated Chargeable Income (ECI) Filing](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/estimated-chargeable-income-(eci)-filing)

What is the Ordinary Wage (OW) ceiling?
The Ordinary Wage (OW) ceiling sets the maximum amount of OW that attracts CPF contributions in a calendar month for all employees. It was gradually raised and has reached $8,000 in 2026. The increase took place in four steps, as shown in the table below, to allow employers and employees to adjust to the changes.
Table: Changes in CPF salary ceilings
CPF Ordinary Wage ceiling | CPF annual salary ceiling
From 1 Jan 2016 to 31 Aug 2023 | $6,000 | $102,000 (no change)
From 1 Sep to 31 Dec 2023 | $6,300 (+$300)
From 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2024 | $6,800 (+$500)
From 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2025 | $7,400 (+$600)
From 1 Jan 2026 | $8,000 (+$600)

**Source:** Examples for computation of Additional Wage (AW) Ceiling (live external)

The AW ceiling determines the maximum amount of AW subject to CPF contributions for the year. An employee’s AW ceiling is computed on a
per employer, per year basis. The AW ceiling applies to all Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents (SPR).
AW ceiling Calculation
The AW ceiling is computed using the following formula:
$102,000 - Total Ordinary Wages (OW) subject to CPF for the year
For the year 2026, the AW ceiling is
$102,000 – ($8,000* x 12)
* The OW ceiling is capped at $8,000 for 2026.
Note: The applicable AW ceiling depends on the due and payable date of the AW. For example, if the 2025 bonus is due and payable to the employee in 2026, then the employer should contribute
according to the 2026 AW ceiling.
Step 1: At every AW payment, e mployers should estimate the AW ceiling by using the current year’s estimated monthly OW. Employers should
either:
a) Submit a refund application online (select the option: Refund of payments made for 1 employee/platform worker) immediately if any excess
contributions on AW are detected; or
b) Pay the shortfall in contributions on AW, if any.
Step 2: In the last month of employment or end of the year in December (whichever is earlier), employers should re-calculate the AW
ceiling based on the actual OW subject to CPF paid up till the last month of employment or in December and pay any shortfall in CPF contributions
together with the employee's contributions for his last month of employment or in December. If there are any excess CPF contributions, you
should submit a refund application online.
For the examples below, we assume that the monthly contribution rates applicable for the employee is for Singaporeans and SPRs (from third
year and onwards). If your employee is a SPR in the first or second year of SPR status, please use the applicable monthly contribution rates.

rows.question: What information determines the CPF contribution rate for an employee?
rows.before:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### CPF Board — CPF contributions

**Status:** Evidence verified

**Employee and employer CPF contribution rate factors** (party in scope: Employer)
- **CPF rule explanation:** CPF contribution rates depend on citizenship or permanent-resident status (including the applicable PR year), age group, and total wages or wage band. Use the rate table effective for the contribution period being assessed. For employees in their first two years of permanent-resident status, the employer and employee may jointly apply for a higher contribution rate under CPF’s options. This is a general explanation and does not determine an employee’s rate or calculate contributions. [CPF | How much CPF contributions to pay](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay)

**Source:** CPF | How much CPF contributions to pay (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Employee and employer CPF contribution rate factors): CPF contribution rates vary based on your employee’s citizenship status, age group, and total wages. As an employer, you are required to pay CPF contributions for your employees who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents and who are earning total wages of more than $50 per month.
Step 1: Select the contribution rate table based on citizenship status
Select the contribution rate table that applies to your employee.
Table 1: Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) from the third year of SPR status
Table 2: SPR in the first year of SPR status
Table 3: SPR in the second year of SPR status
Please ensure that your employees inform you the date when they became Singapore Citizens or SPRs, as different CPF contribution rates are applicable.
Determine the year of SPR status
The first year begins on the day of SPR conversion
The second year begins on the first day of the month after the first anniversary of SPR conversion
The third year begins on the first day of the month after the second anniversary of SPR conversion
Contribute more for first and second year SPRs
You and your employee who is in the first two years of SPR status can jointly apply to contribute CPF at a higher rate. The options are:
You and your employee both contribute at full rates (Table 1)
You contribute at full rates while your employee continues to contribute at graduated rates (Tables 4 and 5)
Step 2: Determine the rates based on age group and wage band
Different rates apply to different age groups.
New contribution rates apply from the first day of the month after the employee’s 55th, 60th, 65th or 70th birthday.
Different rates apply for different wage bands.
- Official source: [CPF | How much CPF contributions to pay](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/how-much-cpf-contributions-to-pay)

Updates on 21 May 2026
To further strengthen the retirement adequacy of senior employees, there will be an increase to the CPF contribution rates from 1 Jan 2027. Find out more about these changes and how it affects you and your employees.
Current rates
What are the CPF contribution rates?
The following table summarises the current contribution rates for Singaporeans and SPRs (from third year and onwards) with monthly wages above $750, across the different age groups.
Employee’s age (years) | Contribution rates from 1 January 2026 (monthly wages > $750)
By employer (% of wage) | By employee (% of wage) | Total (% of wage)
55 and below | 17 | 20 | 37
Above 55 to 60 | 16 | 18 | 34
Above 60 to 65 | 12.5 | 12.5 | 25
Above 65 to 70 | 9 | 7.5 | 16.5
Above 70 | 7.5 | 5 | 12.5
View all tables (PDF, 0.2MB) for the full set of contribution rate tables covering all citizenship statuses and SPR years.
Computation
Determine your employees’ CPF contributions
CPF contribution rates vary based on your employee’s citizenship status, age group, and total wages. As an employer, you are required to pay CPF contributions for your employees who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents and who are earning total wages of more than $50 per month.
Step 1: Select the contribution rate table based on citizenship status
Select the contribution rate table that applies to your employee.
Table 1: Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) from the third year of SPR status
Table 2: SPR in the first year of SPR status
Table 3: SPR in the second year of SPR status
Please ensure that your employees inform you the date when they became Singapore Citizens or SPRs, as different CPF contribution rates are applicable.
Determine the year of SPR status
The first year begins on the day of SPR conversion
The second year begins on the first day of the month after the first anniversary of SPR conversion
The third year begins on the first day of the month after the second anniversary of SPR conversion
Contribute more for first and second year SPRs
You and your employee who is in the first two years of SPR status can jointly apply to contribute CPF at a higher rate. The options are:
You and your employee both contribute at full rates (Table 1)
You contribute at full rates while your employee continues to contribute at graduated rates (Tables 4 and 5)
Step 2: Determine the rates based on age group and wage band
Different rates apply to different age groups.
New contribution rates apply from the first day of the month after the employee’s 55th, 60th, 65th or 70th birthday.
Different rates apply for different wage bands.
Step 3: Determine the Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
Apply the wage ceilings to determine Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
An employee’s CPF contributions are computed based on the Total Wages payable in a calendar month.
Total Wages are made up of an employee’s Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages. Different ceilings apply to Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages.
Step 4: Compute the CPF contributions on Total Wages
Compute Total CPF contributions
You can compute the total CPF contributions by applying the contribution rate to your employee’s total wages subject to CPF. The total CPF contributions comprise both your share as the employer and your employee’s share, which you are required to pay to the CPF Board. You are entitled to recover the employee’s share when paying your employee’s wages for the month.
Note that if your employee earns above $50 but not more than $500 per month, there is no employee’s share of CPF contributions. You will still need to pay the employer’s share.
Round off your Total CPF contributions
Please round off the Total CPF contributions to the nearest dollar. Cents should be dropped for amounts less than 50 cents, and amounts of 50 cents and above should be treated as an additional dollar. The cents should always be dropped for the employee’s share of CPF contributions.

The following table summarises the current contribution rates for Singaporeans and SPRs (from third year and onwards) with monthly wages above $750, across the different age groups.
Employee’s age (years) | Contribution rates from 1 January 2026 (monthly wages > $750)
By employer (% of wage) | By employee (% of wage) | Total (% of wage)
55 and below | 17 | 20 | 37
Above 55 to 60 | 16 | 18 | 34
Above 60 to 65 | 12.5 | 12.5 | 25
Above 65 to 70 | 9 | 7.5 | 16.5
Above 70 | 7.5 | 5 | 12.5
View all tables (PDF, 0.2MB) for the full set of contribution rate tables covering all citizenship statuses and SPR years.
Computation
Determine your employees’ CPF contributions
CPF contribution rates vary based on your employee’s citizenship status, age group, and total wages. As an employer, you are required to pay CPF contributions for your employees who are Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents and who are earning total wages of more than $50 per month.
Step 1: Select the contribution rate table based on citizenship status
Select the contribution rate table that applies to your employee.
Table 1: Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) from the third year of SPR status
Table 2: SPR in the first year of SPR status
Table 3: SPR in the second year of SPR status
Please ensure that your employees inform you the date when they became Singapore Citizens or SPRs, as different CPF contribution rates are applicable.
Determine the year of SPR status
The first year begins on the day of SPR conversion
The second year begins on the first day of the month after the first anniversary of SPR conversion
The third year begins on the first day of the month after the second anniversary of SPR conversion
Contribute more for first and second year SPRs
You and your employee who is in the first two years of SPR status can jointly apply to contribute CPF at a higher rate. The options are:
You and your employee both contribute at full rates (Table 1)
You contribute at full rates while your employee continues to contribute at graduated rates (Tables 4 and 5)
Step 2: Determine the rates based on age group and wage band
Different rates apply to different age groups.
New contribution rates apply from the first day of the month after the employee’s 55th, 60th, 65th or 70th birthday.
Different rates apply for different wage bands.
Step 3: Determine the Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
Apply the wage ceilings to determine Total Wages subject to CPF contributions
An employee’s CPF contributions are computed based on the Total Wages payable in a calendar month.
Total Wages are made up of an employee’s Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages. Different ceilings apply to Ordinary Wages and Additional Wages.
Step 4: Compute the CPF contributions on Total Wages
Compute Total CPF contributions
You can compute the total CPF contributions by applying the contribution rate to your employee’s total wages subject to CPF. The total CPF contributions comprise both your share as the employer and your employee’s share, which you are required to pay to the CPF Board. You are entitled to recover the employee’s share when paying your employee’s wages for the month.
Note that if your employee earns above $50 but not more than $500 per month, there is no employee’s share of CPF contributions. You will still need to pay the employer’s share.
Round off your Total CPF contributions
Please round off the Total CPF contributions to the nearest dollar. Cents should be dropped for amounts less than 50 cents, and amounts of 50 cents and above should be treated as an additional dollar. The cents should always be dropped for the employee’s share of CPF contributions.

The AW ceiling determines the maximum amount of AW subject to CPF contributions for the year. An employee’s AW ceiling is computed on a
per employer, per year basis. The AW ceiling applies to all Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents (SPR).
AW ceiling Calculation
The AW ceiling is computed using the following formula:
$102,000 - Total Ordinary Wages (OW) subject to CPF for the year
For the year 2026, the AW ceiling is
$102,000 – ($8,000* x 12)
* The OW ceiling is capped at $8,000 for 2026.

according to the 2026 AW ceiling.

contributions on AW are detected; or

#### ACRA — Corporate filing and governance

**Status:** Verified evidence; case application unresolved

**Company AGM timing requirements and deadline inputs** (party in scope: Company)
- **ACRA rule explanation:** ACRA’s current guidance states that, for financial years ending on or after 31 August 2018, listed companies generally hold an AGM within four months after FYE and non-listed companies within six months. A private company may be exempt if it sends its financial statements to all members within five months after FYE, or if it is dormant, not listed (and not a subsidiary of a listed company), and has assets of S$500,000 or less (consolidated for an ultimate parent). It may also dispense with an AGM by a resolution passed by all members. Even then, a member can request an AGM up to 14 days before the six-month deadline; the company must hold it within six months after FYE. A member or auditor may request a general meeting within 14 days of receiving the financial statements, and the company must hold that meeting within 14 days of the request. The page says an extension application must be made before the due date but does not state its duration or all conditions. AGM details must be declared in the annual return even if no AGM was held. A specific conclusion depends on FYE, listing/private status, dormancy, group status, assets, delivery of statements, resolutions, requests and any extension application. **Private-company small-company audit exemption criteria** (party in scope: Company)
- **ACRA rule explanation:** Small-company audit exemption requires the entity to be a private company in the financial year and to meet at least two of the three quantitative criteria for each of the immediate past two consecutive financial years: revenue no more than S$10 million, assets no more than S$10 million, or no more than 50 full-time employees at FYE. A company that is less than two years old is assessed against criteria in its current year. A group also has to meet the separate consolidated small-group criteria. Two of three criteria must hold for both immediately preceding consecutive financial years for an established company; “this year and last year” does not always establish that period. The Singapore company and the entire group (including foreign entities) must each satisfy their respective test where the company is part of a group. A qualifying company remains qualified until it ceases to be private or no longer meets at least two criteria over the immediate past two consecutive financial years. The current-year test applies to a newly incorporated private company less than two years old. A separate dormant-company audit exemption may apply; do not confuse audit exemption with relief from preparing financial statements or filing an annual return. A case-specific conclusion requires: Private-company status during the financial year. Revenue, total assets and full-time employee count for the immediate past two consecutive financial years. If part of a group, the consolidated figures and entire-group scope. Whether the company is newly incorporated or another audit exception is being considered. A company-specific conclusion needs two financial years’ facts and, for a group, consolidated facts. Audit exemption does not exempt a company from keeping proper records, preparing financial statements, annual-return filing or tax filing. - **ACRA rule explanation:** Small-company audit exemption requires the entity to be a private company in the financial year and to meet at least two of the three quantitative criteria for each of the immediate past two consecutive financial years: revenue no more than S$10 million, assets no more than S$10 million, or no more than 50 full-time employees at FYE. A company that is less than two years old is assessed against criteria in its current year. A group also has to meet the separate consolidated small-group criteria. Two of three criteria must hold for both immediately preceding consecutive financial years for an established company; “this year and last year” does not always establish that period. The Singapore company and the entire group (including foreign entities) must each satisfy their respective test where the company is part of a group. A qualifying company remains qualified until it ceases to be private or no longer meets at least two criteria over the immediate past two consecutive financial years. The current-year test applies to a newly incorporated private company less than two years old. A separate dormant-company audit exemption may apply; do not confuse audit exemption with relief from preparing financial statements or filing an annual return. A case-specific conclusion requires: Private-company status during the financial year. Revenue, total assets and full-time employee count for the immediate past two consecutive financial years. If part of a group, the consolidated figures and entire-group scope. Whether the company is newly incorporated or another audit exception is being considered. A company-specific conclusion needs two financial years’ facts and, for a group, consolidated facts. Audit exemption does not exempt a company from keeping proper records, preparing financial statements, annual-return filing or tax filing. •

◦

•

◦

◦ Total assets of $10 million or less, based on your financial statements prepared in accordance with the accounting standards

◦

•

◦

◦ 50 employees or fewer, based on the number of full-time employees at the end of your financial year

◦

•

If your company is newly incorporated (less than two years old)

You qualify for audit exemption if you meet the criteria in the current financial year.

•

• First financial year: Check if you are a private company and meet two out of three quantitative criteria that year.

•

•

• Second financial year: If you did not qualify in the first year, check again using the same requirements for the second year.

•

If your company is part of a group

You need to meet both of these conditions to qualify for audit exemption:

•

• Your Singapore company or subsidiary qualifies as a small company; and

•

•

• Your entire group (including foreign entities) meets at least two of these quantitative criteria for the immediate past two consecutive financial years:

•

◦

◦ Total annual revenue of $10 million or less, based on your holding company's consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with the accounting standards

◦

•

◦

◦ Total assets of $10 million or less, based on your holding company's consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with the accounting standards

◦

•

◦

◦ 50 employees or fewer, based on the number of full-time employees at the end of your financial year

◦

•

Note: The audit exemption applies to financial years beginning on or after 1 July 2015.

Maintaining your exemption status

Once your company qualifies as a small company, you remain qualified in subsequent financial years unless:

•

• You cease to be a private company at any time during a financial year; or

•

•

• You do not meet at least two out of three criteria for the immediate past two consecutive financial years

•

**Annual return officer particulars confirmation from 20 October 2026** (party in scope: Company)
- **ACRA rule explanation:** From 20 October 2026, an annual-return filer must confirm that current particulars already provided to ACRA are accurate for directors, chief executive officers (CEOs), secretaries, auditors and relevant members. These particulars include names, identification details, nationality, contact address, appointment dates, registered office address and shareholding details where applicable. The form separately asks whether any individual performs the CEO role. A company limited by guarantee must confirm its latest-reported total member count. Applies to annual returns filed from the expressly stated commencement date. Check ACRA-recorded particulars and update inaccurate particulars in Bizfile before filing. The CEO question concerns individuals performing the role; the ACRA notice does not limit it to a title or appointed position. Companies limited by guarantee have an additional total-number-of-members confirmation. The notice does not say the CEO question or officer-particulars confirmation changes the underlying duty to appoint or register officers. A case-specific conclusion requires: For a particular filing: filing date, company type, existing ACRA particulars, whether individuals perform the CEO role, and whether the company is limited by guarantee. General change explanation only; does not verify what particulars are currently recorded for an entity. Do not apply this change to filings submitted before 20 October 2026 without contemporaneous evidence. The notice gives examples of particulars and says “where applicable”; it is not a field-by-field eform schema. The notice states that the new change applies from 20 October 2026; it does not establish what requirements governed filings before that date. - **ACRA rule explanation:** A company secretary must be appointed within six months of successful company registration, and the position cannot be vacant for more than six months. ### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence is incomplete for one or more material issues.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.

**Material evidence gaps:** See the evidence gaps and coverage limitations below.

#### Monetary Authority of Singapore — Financial regulation

**Status:** Verified evidence; case application unresolved

**Simplified VCFM licensing path and admission eligibility** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** At a high level, MAS describes a VCFM as an LFMC that operates under a simplified VCFM regime. A company that solely manages venture capital funds may apply to use this route. MAS says VCFMs follow simplified admission criteria; the cited page points to Appendix 4 but does not give a full side-by-side comparison or its detailed criteria. The route requires an application and is not automatic eligibility. MAS also considers the business model and risks, risk and compliance controls, track record and expertise, fitness and propriety, minimum financial requirements, and dedicated secure office arrangements; check Appendix 4 before deciding whether a particular manager qualifies. [Fund Management Licensing | Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) (offline fixture title)](https://www.mas.gov.sg/regulation/capital-markets/apply-for-licensing-or-registration-of-capital-market-entities/fund-management-licensing)
- **Application unresolved:** For Simplified VCFM licensing path and admission eligibility, case-specific treatment or calculation has not been verified. The relevant facts and statutory conditions still need to be established.

**Source:** Fund Management Licensing | Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) (offline fixture title) (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Simplified VCFM licensing path and admission eligibility): If your company solely manages venture capital funds, it may apply to be an LFMC that operates under the simplified venture capital fund manager (VCFM) regime.

Individuals performing key functions in a fund management company, such as portfolio construction and allocation, research and advisory, business development and marketing or client servicing are required to be representatives.

You can find out more about fund management activity and the differences between an LFMC and VCFM here.

When we assess your company to be an LFMC or VCFM, MAS considers factors such as:

• Credibility and substantiveness of the business model and plan, and the associated risks;

• Effectiveness of risk management and compliance controls;

• Fund management track record and expertise of an LFMC applicant's management, parent company and major shareholders;

• Fitness and propriety of the applicant, its shareholders and directors; and

• Ability to meet the relevant minimum financial requirements prescribed under the SFA.

In addition, your company needs to operate from a dedicated and secure office space that is accessible only by your company’s directors and staff.

For more information on the admission criteria and applicable requirements, please refer to the Guidelines on Licensing and Conduct of Business for Fund Management Companies.

VCFMs are subject to a simplified set of admission criteria – please refer to Appendix 4 of the aforementioned guidelines.
- Official source: [Fund Management Licensing | Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) (offline fixture title)](https://www.mas.gov.sg/regulation/capital-markets/apply-for-licensing-or-registration-of-capital-market-entities/fund-management-licensing)

rows.question: Are there class exemptions from the fund management licensing requirement?
rows.before:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed, and application to the case remains unresolved.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** Additional case facts or checks are required; see the issue-level limitations.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### Monetary Authority of Singapore — Financial regulation

**Status:** Verified evidence; case application unresolved

**Conditional class exemptions from fund-management licensing** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** A fund manager does not become exempt merely because it manages assets for a related corporation or family member. MAS says a company operating under an existing class exemption does not require a licence, and gives related-corporation or family assets, certain immovable-asset pools, and certain non-capital-markets-product pools for accredited or institutional investors as examples that may be eligible. The specific exemption conditions under section 99 of the SFA and paragraph 5 of the Regulations must be checked before concluding that a particular manager is exempt. [Fund Management Licensing | Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) (offline fixture title)](https://www.mas.gov.sg/regulation/capital-markets/apply-for-licensing-or-registration-of-capital-market-entities/fund-management-licensing)
- **Application unresolved:** For Conditional class exemptions from fund-management licensing, case-specific treatment or calculation has not been verified. The relevant facts and statutory conditions still need to be established.

**Source:** Fund Management Licensing | Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) (offline fixture title) (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Conditional class exemptions from fund-management licensing): If your company is able to operate under an existing class exemption, it does not require a licence. Examples of companies that may be eligible for exemption include those that:

• Manage assets for related corporations or related family members;

• Manage a pool of immovable assets for accredited and institutional investors; or

• Manage a pool of non-capital markets products for accredited and institutional investors.

You can find more information on exemptions under section 99 of the SFA and paragraph 5 of the Second Schedule to the Securities and Futures (Licensing and Conduct of Business) Regulations.

- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports QDC filing requirement for a venture capital fund manager): If your company solely manages venture capital funds, it may apply to be an LFMC that operates under the simplified venture capital fund manager (VCFM) regime.

Individuals performing key functions in a fund management company, such as portfolio construction and allocation, research and advisory, business development and marketing or client servicing are required to be representatives.

You can find out more about fund management activity and the differences between an LFMC and VCFM here.

When we assess your company to be an LFMC or VCFM, MAS considers factors such as:

• Credibility and substantiveness of the business model and plan, and the associated risks;

• Effectiveness of risk management and compliance controls;

• Fund management track record and expertise of an LFMC applicant's management, parent company and major shareholders;

• Fitness and propriety of the applicant, its shareholders and directors; and

• Ability to meet the relevant minimum financial requirements prescribed under the SFA.

In addition, your company needs to operate from a dedicated and secure office space that is accessible only by your company’s directors and staff.

For more information on the admission criteria and applicable requirements, please refer to the Guidelines on Licensing and Conduct of Business for Fund Management Companies.

VCFMs are subject to a simplified set of admission criteria – please refer to Appendix 4 of the aforementioned guidelines.
